context: Define the first reusable MC Legends prototype-lab foundation without coupling experimental gameplay code to the production web repository or pre-empting unresolved MCL-1 engine/product-format governance.
hard_constraints: HC-001 no standalone game engine or Minecraft loader selection before MCL-1/governance clearance
HC-002 no runtime dependency on the production web app/backend
HC-003 prototypes must remain disposable and isolated
HC-004 prototype design status must not silently become canon
HC-005 asset provenance and stable ids are required
HC-006 no production backend/cloud infrastructure in the first prototype foundation

candidates.name: Separate engine-neutral prototype-lab repository
candidates.summary: A dedicated repository contains experiment contracts, asset registry, validation, agent rules and an empty runtime-adapter slot. Actual engine integration is deferred until the governance gate clears.
risks: A separate repository can drift from MLOA decisions if source references are not maintained.
Runtime remains non-playable until an adapter is approved.
non_risks: Does not alter the existing web CI/deployment unit.
Can be deleted without changing production web behavior.
sensitivity_points: whether a prototype-runtime exception is approved
how many mechanics actually repeat across experiments
tradeoff_points: Maximum isolation and disposability versus one additional repository to govern.

candidates.name: Prototype workspace inside DYAI2025/MC_legends
candidates.summary: Add a prototype package below the existing web repository and adjust root TypeScript/ESLint/CI boundaries to isolate it.

hard_constraint_results.notes: Only if no engine is selected yet.
Same repository and root tooling create avoidable coupling even if runtime dependencies are separated.

risks: Root tsconfig includes all TypeScript files recursively, so prototype files enter existing typecheck scope unless the production toolchain is changed.
Existing CI is production-web specific and would gain experimental churn.
non_risks: One repository simplifies discovery and source linking.
sensitivity_points: Whether repository-wide tooling can be changed without slowing web delivery.
tradeoff_points: Single-repo discoverability versus blast-radius and CI coupling.

candidates.name: Choose PlayCanvas/Godot/Unity now and scaffold executable runtime
candidates.summary: Create a real 3D runtime immediately with third-person controller, local play and asset loading.

hard_constraint_results.notes: MCL-1 is still open and repository instructions explicitly prohibit engine selection.

risks: Would silently convert a prototype-tool preference into a project engine decision under current governance.
non_risks: Would produce the fastest path to an immediately playable 3D scene after governance clearance.
tradeoff_points: Immediate playability versus explicit project decision integrity.

strongest_counterargument: A separate repository creates another place to maintain and may encourage duplicate contracts; a carefully isolated workspace in the existing repository could keep all project knowledge together. This becomes decisive only if repository/tooling coupling is explicitly accepted and CI can exclude prototype churn without weakening production gates.
decision_rationale: The existing repository is now an active production-oriented web system with PostgreSQL, CI and deployment work, not an empty bootstrap.
The root TypeScript configuration includes all TypeScript files recursively, making an embedded prototype package non-isolated by default.
Confluence explicitly treats the current Next.js architecture as web-only and keeps game technology open.
The visual asset design already supports a registry/provenance approach that can be reused without coupling runtimes.
A separate disposable lab best matches rapid experimentation and low migration cost.
rejected_alternatives: CAND-002 remains possible but is inferior while the web repository has global TypeScript and web-specific CI scope.
CAND-003 is blocked until MCL-1 or an explicit non-canonical prototype-runtime exception clears engine selection.
consequences: Prototype experiments live outside the production web repository.
The first foundation can be created as contracts, schemas, docs and validation without selecting an engine.
A runtime adapter is a later controlled decision, not an implicit part of this concept.
Shared mechanic modules are not created speculatively; promotion requires demonstrated reuse.
Prototype outcomes can inform MCL design decisions but do not write canon automatically.

risks.statement: Runtime playability is delayed while engine selection is blocked.
risks.mitigation: Resolve MCL-1 or approve a narrowly scoped disposable prototype-runtime exception.

risks.statement: A separate lab can drift from Confluence design status.
risks.mitigation: Require source_refs and design_status in every experiment contract.

risks.statement: Premature shared-mechanic abstraction could slow experiments.
risks.mitigation: Default all logic to experiment-local; promote only after reuse in at least two experiments.

risks.statement: Third-party assets can introduce license/provenance ambiguity.
risks.mitigation: Require license/source/provenance fields in the asset registry before runtime use.

assumptions.statement: The prototype lab is a disposable learning system and is not intended to evolve into the production game repository.
assumptions.review_trigger: The user explicitly changes the purpose from prototype lab to production foundation.

assumptions.statement: Third-person remains the preferred first playable perspective.
assumptions.review_trigger: The user selects a different camera for the first experiment.

review_triggers: The first runtime adapter is researched and validated
Two experiments need the same mechanic
Prototype work begins modifying production web files
migration_signals: Promote an experiment-local mechanic to shared only after at least two experiments depend on the same behavior contract.
Create a production-game architecture only after product-format and engine decisions are explicitly made.
